output.headline: McKesson has bought in the target's own sub-sector and paid 25.1x, but with one deal and none in the target's region, conviction is low.
output.differentiator: Paid 25.1x on its one Health IT deal, above every other buyer on the priority list, and the deal was $405M, the largest median deal on the list. Single-deal evidence. [D:MA-2017-0106]
output.why_them: Health IT bolt-on precedent; paid highest multiple on the list

acquirer_overview.title: A very large strategic with one closed Health IT deal on file
points: Strategic buyer with Health IT as its home sub-sector; one deal in the file (2017), and it closed [B:buyer, K:closed_share].
Annual revenue of $403,430M for the fiscal year ending 2026-03-31, far larger than a $300M target [P:1].
Recent filings show an 80% interest in PRISM Vision for $875M and a 70% interest in Core Ventures for $2.5B, both physician practices [P:2].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Own-sub-sector focus and margin fit support a bolt-on, on thin evidence
points: Share of deals in the target's sub-sector is the strongest factor, and target margin close to what it usually buys is a strong factor [S:sector_share, S:margin_fit].
Its one deal was tagged Platform Build and Technology Capability, the latter on just 10% of deals in the file, so it has bought for capability [M:platform_build, M:technology_capability].
Having bought from this kind of seller before is a slight factor against; a deal no bigger than its past one is a slight factor for [S:own_fit_s, S:not_bigger].

precedent_activity.title: One relevant precedent: a $405M Health IT bolt-on in 2017
points: Bought Southeast Medical Informatics in 2017: $405M bolt-on at 25.1x EBITDA and 5.40x revenue, closed [D:MA-2017-0106, K:median_ev_revenue].
The deal sits in the $150M-$600M comparable size band, the same band as this target [K:size_band].
No deals since 2022, and its only deal was in the Southwest, not nationally [K:recent, K:by_region].

valuation_context.title: Median multiple is defensible; McKesson has paid above the top quartile
points: 13 comparable same-sub-sector deals: 19.4x at the 25th percentile, 21.4x median, 23.3x at the 75th [V:comps].
Margin of 25.0% is above the comps' median of 22.2% but not in the top quarter, so the 50th percentile is the anchor [V:comps].
Its own 25.1x median paid exceeds the comps' 75th percentile; cost synergy headroom is $14M-$23M [V:comps, V:synergy].

risk_flags.title: Thin Health IT record
risk_flags.concern: Only one deal in the target's sub-sector, in 2017, so appetite today is unproven.
risk_flags.mitigant: That deal closed, in the same sub-sector and size band, at a high multiple.
risk_flags.reality: Conviction stays Low because the basis is a single deal [T:record, C:conviction].

risk_flags.title: No deal in the target's region
risk_flags.concern: Its one deal was in the Southwest; none in the National region.
risk_flags.mitigant: Its 10-K describes operations across North America.
risk_flags.reality: Footprint is stated, but no regional deal precedent supports it [K:by_region, P:4].

risk_flags.title: Competing capital priorities
risk_flags.concern: Practice acquisitions and a Medical-Surgical separation may absorb management attention and capital.
risk_flags.mitigant: Revenue of $403,430M gives ample balance-sheet scale.
risk_flags.reality: It ranks 10th on the priority list, so it is a long-shot call [P:1, P:2, P:3, R:rank].

conviction.rationale: Only one deal in the target's own sub-sector and none in its region. The sub-sector share is the strongest factor, but a single 2017 precedent is too thin for higher conviction. [C:conviction, T:record]
